raw_description: At Octopus Energy Trading, we’re on a mission to reshape the future of energy. As part of Octopus Energy Group, we’re creating an innovative approach to trading that will accelerate the transition to a Net Zero world. With the growth of renewables and a push toward decarbonising heating and transport, greater flexibility in the grid is essential. We are building cutting-edge technology to optimise everything, from domestic EV charging to grid-scale batteries, to meet the global demand for energy flexibility. We’re looking for passionate and unconventional thinkers to join us on this journey, bringing a diversity of experience and ideas to shape a more efficient, flexible, and sustainable energy system. With an increase in variable and distributed supply, using data for trading and forecasting has never been more important. Octopus has always had a tech-first approach, and our trading and analytics tools are all built in-house by specialised domain teams, focussed on areas like grid-scale batteries or market fundamentals, all building on a common platform that is managed by our core engineering team. We are seeking a software engineer to join the core engineering team and help own the developer experience. raw_description: Reports to: Head of Communications - Preferred location: Europe or Asia (GMT +/- 7 hours) - Annual Salary: Compensation for this role is benchmarked at EUR 73,000 and adjusted based on the employee’s location and aligned local salary bands. - Working Hours: Full time role at 5 days/week About Climate Catalyst Climate Catalyst is a non-profit dedicated to galvanizing the collective power of business, investors, and civil society to influence and accelerate policy change in Asia and Europe. Our vision is a just, prosperous world in which global warming is limited to 1.5°C. Climate Catalyst works to strengthen collaboration and mobilise new actors on pivotal climate challenges in heavy emitting industries. We build power and compel political leaders to act at the speed and scale needed to tackle the climate crisis. We do this by: - Working behind the scenes with stakeholders in Europe and Asia to identify critical climate issues where action to date has been limited, and the potential for collaboration is high. - Bringing together renowned experts and new entrants to share ideas, and design and deliver creative campaigns that secure decisive changes in national and regional policy to deliver sectoral tipping points and secure significant emissions reductions. - Advising on strategy, offering grants and bringing creative communications, advocacy and business expertise to build power across the climate community and catalyse action. To date, we’ve used this model successfully to mobilise the business community in support of the EU Nature Restoration Law, the first legislation for peatlands protection across Europe, and spark collective action in India that led to a commitment from the Ministry of Steel to develop a green steel roadmap. About the role Communications and narrative building is a core part of Climate Catalyst’s model for impact. This role will be instrumental in delivering impactful and exciting digital communications that support our programmes delivery impact - by informing, influencing and inspiring action. It will also contribute to building Climate Catalyst’s reputation with our key stakeholders across Europe, Asia and globally. You will build our presence and impact by developing digital communication strategies to support our programmes in Europe, India and Indonesia, managing our digital channels and supporting colleagues to grow their online presence. It will support our already established programmes of work on aviation and chemicals in Europe and steel in Asia and support the team with digital expertise as we grow new programmes of work. Climate Catalyst commits to deliver our communications for and through partners. Therefore this role will not only support our internal teams, but with partners across our networks and coalitions to co-build strategies for collective impact. You will also support the Head of Communications in building and protecting the Climate Catalyst brand. What you will do Strategy: - Contribute to Climate Catalyst’s overall communications strategy. - Lead the development of impactful digital strategies to support programme teams to deliver impact across Europe and Asia, including reporting and evaluation. - Advise colleagues on social media best practice, supporting them to grow their professional profiles. - Work with partners and Climate Catalyst coalitions to co-build shared digital strategies and to share and drive digital best practice across the wider ecosystems in which we work. - Manage and monitor Climate Catalyst’s own digital channels - including website and social media - and regularly suggest ways to improve and enhance our digital presence. - Lead the development of thought leadership and reputation building content to help establish Climate Catalyst and its staff as trusted experts in energising collective action on pivotal climate challenges. - Lead and implement SEO strategy, working with the wider team to improve the visibility and performance of our learning hub. Content development: - Lead the content creation for Climate Catalyst’s digital channels, including imagery, graphics, simple reports and briefings and videos, using tools like Canva. - Write and edit copy for Climate Catalyst’s digital channels, including the website, email, newsletters, social media and other digital products. - Lead on scheduling and posting of social media content, and interact with responses. - Keep all templates -date and develop new ones where needed. - Maintain Climate Catalyst’ brand assets, including our image library, icon and graphic library etc. Administration: - Help ensure all digital and communication outputs are on brand, and support teams to meet best practice for brand consistency. - Help ensure Climate Catalyst is meeting best practice standards for digital communications. - Support budget management of digital activities. - Support team with monitoring and reporting requests, and keep our internal dashboard up to day to showcase digital impact. - Support the team to ensure compliance with data protection regulations, and ensure use of tools - i.e. HubSpot, in line with these regulations. - Manage relationships with external consultants and agencies where needed. Innovation and learning: - Keep on top of trends and identify opportunities for experimentation in digital output. - Run internal and partner learning sessions to support broader growth of digital expertise and best practice

Si vous recherchez un autre domaine d’intérêt général, veuillez consulter les autres postes pour universitaires sur notre site Web! À propos d’EDC: À Exportation et développement Canada (EDC), nous aidons les entreprises canadiennes à réussir à l’étranger. En tant que société d’État à vocation financière, EDC propose des solutions financières innovantes et des conseils d’experts pour aider les entreprises à explorer de nouveaux marchés, à atténuer leurs risques et à se développer. Pourquoi vous joindre à EDC? - Collaborez avec une équipe diversifiée et expérimentée. - Épanouissez-vous dans un environnement axé sur le soutien et le travail d’équipe. - Influencez les communautés à l’échelle mondiale en stimulant la croissance durable des marchés émergents. - Travaillez dans une entreprise reconnue comme l’un des 100 meilleurs employeurs du Canada, l’un des meilleurs employeurs pour la diversité au Canada et l’un des employeurs canadiens favorisant le plus la conciliation travail-famille. - Profitez d’un programme d’avantages globaux comprenant des avantages sociaux, des congés, des programmes de bien-être et des occasions de perfectionnement professionnel. Offre d’emploi pour les personnes étudiantes et nouvellement diplômées: Nos offres d’emploi pour les personnes étudiantes et nouvellement diplômées comprennent des stages et des programmes d’alternance travail-études, tous conçus pour donner un bon départ à votre carrière. Un stage supplémentaire de quatre mois ou plus peut s’ajouter au stage d’automne de quatre mois pendant la nouvelle année civile, selon les besoins opérationnels. Le travail est normalement effectué à temps plein, mais il existe une certaine flexibilité en matière de travail à temps partiel. Notre programme est idéal pour les étudiantes et les étudiants et pour les professionnelles et les professionnels en début de carrière qui sont nouvellement diplômés et ont terminé leurs cours l’année dernière. Les stages effectués dans le cadre de notre programme peuvent faire partie d’un programme coopératif (COOP) universitaire accrédité. Nous recrutons activement des professionnelles et professionnels en début de carrière pour la session d’automne 2026 dans diverses équipes à la recherche de en marketing et communications personnes étudiantes ou nouvellement diplômées. Les mandats des équipes varient, donc si l’on vous convoque à une entrevue, vous recevrez une description détaillée. Postulez à une banque de candidature si vous êtes une personne étudiante ou nouvellement diplômée diplômé qui: - suit actuellement ou a récemment terminé un programme en marketing ou en communications; - suit actuellement un programme connexe et s’intéresse à des postes dans le domaine du marketing et des communications; - souhaite acquérir un éventail de compétences au sein d’équipes responsables de la marque, des relations internes, des communications, de la stratégie marketing et de la technologie du marketing, notamment. Profil de l’étudiante idéale ou de l’étudiant idéal: - Diplôme d’un programme de premier ou de deuxième cycle (jusqu’à un an après la date d’obtention du diplôme) ou diplôme en voie d’obtention - Disponibilité pour une période de 8 mois ou plus – Bien que les stages ont une durée de 4 mois, la préférence sera accordée aux candidates et candidats disponibles jusqu’en 2027 - Expérience professionnelle antérieure liée au domaine d’études - Aptitudes marquées pour la communication orale et écrite - Motivation, sens de l’initiative, de l’organisation et de l’analyse - Capacité de travailler de façon autonome dans une équipe - Enthousiasme dans l’exécution des tâches simples comme complexes - La connaissance des deux langues officielles est un atout, mais peut être exigée pour certains postes Aperçu d’un stage étudiant à EDC: C’est l’occasion de tisser des relations avec des collègues provenant de secteurs divers et variés, mais aussi de déceler et de concrétiser des occasions d’amélioration et d’innovation. C’est apprendre et se perfectionner auprès des membres de la Société en profitant d’un programme d’encadrement et de mentorat. C’est évoluer dans un environnement ultraproductif, souple et dynamique et misant sur les technologies depuis nos carrefours communautaires des quatre coins du Canada. À quoi s’attendre de la part d’EDC: - Vous recevrez un avis lorsque nous aurons reçu votre demande. - Si votre profil correspond aux besoins d’une équipe, nous communiquerons avec vous pour fixer un entretien avec celle‑ci. Vous recevrez une description de l’équipe pour laquelle votre candidature a été sélectionnée en préparation de votre entretien. - Nous communiquerons avec les candidates et les candidats de façon continue de juillet à août 2026 pour des entretiens, en fonction de nos besoins opérationnels. Admissibilité: - Les candidates et candidats doivent être des citoyens canadiens, des résidents permanents ou détenir un visa de travail valide au moment de la demande. - Les candidates et candidats doivent satisfaire aux exigences gouvernementales en matière de filtrage de sécurité au niveau requis. - Les candidates et candidats doivent être actuellement inscrits dans un établissement d’enseignement supérieur ou avoir terminé leurs études au cours de la dernière année. Détails de la rémunération: Les salaires des étudiants, des nouveaux diplômés et des titulaires d'une maîtrise varient entre 42 900 $ et 56 550 $ par an, en fonction de l'année d'études. Vous trouverez ci-dessous la répartition des salaires par année d'études: - 1ère année: 42 900 $ (22,00 $/heure) - 2ème année: 44 850 $ (23,00 $/heure) - 3ème année: 46 800 $ (24,00 $/heure) - 4ème année et au-delà: 48 750 $ (25,00 $/heure) - Nouveau diplômé (premier cycle): 54 600 $ (28,00 $/heure) - Maîtrise/Doctorat: 56 550 $ (29,00 $/heure) Lieu de travail: - Exportation et développement Canada évolue dans un environnement de travail hybride, avec une exigence actuelle de présence au bureau de deux jours par semaine, laquelle passera à trois jours par semaine à compter de septembre 2026 ( sous réserve de modifications ). - La personne choisie peut travailler à partir du siège social d’EDC à Ottawa ou à partir du Carrefour communautaire à Toronto, à Mississauga, à Montréal, à Brossard, à Laval, à Calgary, à Edmonton, à Halifax ou à Vancouver. Pourquoi vous joindre à EDC? - Collaborez avec une équipe diversifiée et expérimentée. - Épanouissez-vous dans un environnement axé sur le soutien et le travail d’équipe. - Influencez les communautés à l’échelle mondiale en stimulant la croissance durable des marchés émergents. - Travaillez dans une entreprise reconnue comme l’un des 100 meilleurs employeurs du Canada, l’un des meilleurs employeurs pour la diversité au Canada et l’un des employeurs canadiens favorisant le plus la conciliation travail-famille. - Profitez d’un programme d’avantages globaux comprenant des avantages sociaux, des congés, des programmes de bien-être et des occasions de perfectionnement professionnel. Offre d’emploi pour les personnes étudiantes et nouvellement diplômées: Nos offres d’emploi pour les personnes étudiantes et nouvellement diplômées comprennent des stages et des programmes d’alternance travail-études, tous conçus pour donner un bon départ à votre carrière. Un stage supplémentaire de quatre mois ou plus peut s’ajouter au stage d’automne de quatre mois pendant la nouvelle année civile, selon les besoins opérationnels. Le travail est normalement effectué à temps plein, mais il existe une certaine flexibilité en matière de travail à temps partiel. Notre programme est idéal pour les étudiantes et les étudiants et pour les professionnelles et les professionnels en début de carrière qui sont nouvellement diplômés et ont terminé leurs cours l’année dernière. Nous recrutons activement des professionnelles et professionnels en début de carrière pour la session d’automne 2026 dans diverses équipes à la recherche de en marketing et communications personnes étudiantes ou nouvellement diplômées. Postulez à une banque de candidature si vous êtes une personne étudiante ou nouvellement diplômée diplômé qui: - suit actuellement ou a récemment terminé un programme en marketing ou en communications; - suit actuellement un programme connexe et s’intéresse à des postes dans le domaine du marketing et des communications; - souhaite acquérir un éventail de compétences au sein d’équipes responsables de la marque, des relations internes, des communications, de la stratégie marketing et de la technologie du marketing, notamment. Profil de l’étudiante idéale ou de l’étudiant idéal: - Diplôme d’un programme de premier ou de deuxième cycle (jusqu’à un an après la date d’obtention du diplôme) ou diplôme en voie d’obtention - Disponibilité pour une période de 8 mois ou plus – Bien que les stages ont une durée de 4 mois, la préférence sera accordée aux candidates et candidats disponibles jusqu’en 2027 - Expérience professionnelle antérieure liée au domaine d’études - Aptitudes marquées pour la communication orale et écrite - Motivation, sens de l’initiative, de l’organisation et de l’analyse - Capacité de travailler de façon autonome dans une équipe - Enthousiasme dans l’exécution des tâches simples comme complexes - La connaissance des deux langues officielles est un atout, mais peut être exigée pour certains postes Aperçu d’un stage étudiant à EDC: C’est l’occasion de tisser des relations avec des collègues provenant de secteurs divers et variés, mais aussi de déceler et de concrétiser des occasions d’amélioration et d’innovation. C’est apprendre et se perfectionner auprès des membres de la Société en profitant d’un programme d’encadrement et de mentorat. C’est évoluer dans un environnement ultraproductif, souple et dynamique et misant sur les technologies depuis nos carrefours communautaires des quatre coins du Canada. title: Strategic Programs Consultant
pay_candidate_snippets: Momentum partners with innovators and forward-looking organizations working to commercialize advanced energy solutions.
Application Period June 1, 2026 – June 14, 2026
raw_description: Job Summary This externally posted title is intended to better reflect the strategic consulting and sector-specific focus of Momentum’s internal Project Lead role. The Project Lead is a core contributor within the Project Leadership Team, responsible for owning the strategy, quality, and delivery of Momentum’s client projects. Project Leads act as the ultimate authority for their projects, guiding teams, setting direction, and ensuring that client objectives are achieved with excellence. This role is defined by autonomy and accountability. Project Leads determine how budgets are delegated, how teams are structured, and how work is executed. They are expected to be self-sufficient leaders who can translate client goals into actionable strategies, deliver high-quality outcomes, and build enduring client trust. The ideal candidate will bring firsthand experience working with or alongside key federal agencies such as MARAD, DOT, DOE, or the U.S. EPA. This role is best suited for someone who understands how federal infrastructure, transportation, maritime, clean energy, or environmental programs are developed, funded, and implemented within complex agency and public-sector environments. Project Leads play a critical role in business generation by maintaining consistent billable work by selling their own capabilities to Directors internally or by developing new opportunities with existing clients. Duties and Responsibilities - Own project strategy and execution. Lead the development and implementation of project plans that align client objectives with Momentum’s technical, policy, and market expertise. - Serve as the project authority. Act as the primary point of accountability for assigned projects, overseeing scope, budget, and schedule with full decision-making authority unless a Director is directly leading the engagement. - Delegate and manage resources. Determine how project budgets and responsibilities are allocated across Momentum’s internal and external teams, including Client Managers, Project Operations members, and contractors. - Ensure quality and delivery standards. Maintain complete oversight of project quality, deliverables, and client satisfaction. Project Leads are responsible for the success of every output associated with their projects. - Lead multidisciplinary teams. Provide clear direction, feedback, and support to team members, ensuring alignment, workload balance, and effective coordination across functions. - Generate and maintain work. Meet utilization targets through a combination of selling capabilities internally to Directors and deepening relationships with existing clients to secure new scopes of work. - Anticipate and solve problems. Identify delivery challenges early and implement solutions that preserve project quality, client satisfaction, and financial performance. - Mentor through execution. Develop team capabilities through collaborative work, modeling high standards and strong project discipline within each engagement. - Contribute to company growth. Identify emerging client needs and capability gaps that could strengthen Momentum’s offerings and inform future hiring or service expansion. - Build client trust and presence. Serve as the face of Momentum for assigned projects, fostering relationships grounded in credibility and results that make clients view the Project Lead as their trusted partner. - Collaborate cross-functionally. Work closely with Directors, Client Managers, and the Project Operations, and Business Operations teams to align project execution with organizational strategy and performance standards. - Perform other related duties as assigned. Billable Expectation This client-facing position has an 80% utilization rate (1, billable hours annually for full-time workers). Project Leads are responsible for generating and maintaining their own billable workload through client and internal relationships. Supervisory Responsibilities This position does not have formal direct reports but leads project teams composed of Project Operations staff, Client Managers, and other Project Leads. Project Leads provide direction, feedback, and oversight for all project activities and outcomes under their leadership. Reporting Relationship The Project Lead reports to the Vice President, Project Leadership Location This position is remote-eligible. However, due to federal contract requirements or the geographic scope of current projects, the employee may be required to be based in California. The role may require occasional travel to Sacramento and various project sites throughout California and the U.S. Training and onboarding are carried out in person at our Sacramento office. Application Period June 1, 2026 – June 14, 2026 Momentum partners with innovators and forward-looking organizations working to commercialize advanced energy solutions

This role will directly contribute to advancing utility- and government-funded transportation electrification efforts operating across Oregon and Washington. This is an excellent opportunity for professionals looking to build their career in the clean energy space and gain hands-on experience in clean energy program administration. In this role, you will support an existing project delivery team to meet program goals and objectives, including reviewing transportation electrification grant applications, coordinating program activities with partners and clients, and executing on key deliverables. You will add to your skillset by learning firsthand how clean energy programs are administered – from e-bike rebates to transportation electrification grants, and other clean energy projects, this role will grow with your dedication and best-in-class delivery of the programs you’re working to support. The ideal candidate will have experience successfully managing or coordinating programs and/or projects, enjoys working with diverse teams, has excellent time management skills, is highly organized, and can communicate effectively both verbally, and in writing. You have a passion for learning, equitable clean energy access, and a basic understanding of how transportation electrification intersects with environmental justice and community resilience. Building on our expertise in energy efficiency, we're constantly expanding our portfolio of clean energy solutions to guide utilities through increasingly complex, connected challenges. raw_description: Resource Innovations is seeking an Energy Efficiency Program Delivery Analyst to join our growing team in Massachusetts and New Hampshire. This role will blend relationship-driven outreach with program coordination, process optimization, and hands-on project support to help deliver high-performing utility energy efficiency programs. In this highly collaborative role, you will act as a key connector between utility clients, vendors, contractors, and internal teams. You will balance front-end engagement with back-end program execution, helping to onboard and support vendors, move projects forward, and continuously improve the processes and systems that drive program success. This role is well suited for someone with approximately 3+ years of experience who is comfortable taking on a range of responsibilities and making an immediate impact. The right candidate enjoys building relationships, solving problems, improving workflows, and keeping things moving in a fast-paced environment. Success in this role will be measured by strong partner relationships, consistent project momentum, program participation, operational efficiency, excellent communication internally and with client, and the ability to identify and implement process improvements that enhance program performance. Resource Innovations (RI) is a women-led energy transformation firm focused on impact. Building on our expertise in energy efficiency, we're constantly expanding our portfolio of clean energy solutions to guide utilities through increasingly complex, connected challenges. We help organizations build power in their communities in four key ways: we organize a network of values-aligned partners; we provide deep, data-driven insights into people, places, and perspectives; we develop tools that make organizing and engagement easy and more effective; and we offer services that strengthen our partners’ capacity to lead change in their communities. About the Position Murmuration is seeking a highly organized and experienced Senior Project Manager for its Campaigns team. Murmuration’s Campaigns Team helps partners design and execute smarter strategies from the ground up — powered by the best civic data and tools in the country. We provide high-impact consulting and campaign services to local organizations who are closest to solutions. We combine deep campaign expertise with the most advanced civic data infrastructure and offer a full suite of services to help change-makers build power and meet key moments. The Senior Project Manager will report directly to the Senior Manager of Campaign Engagement, working in close partnership to streamline workflows, manage timelines, and mitigate risks across a diverse portfolio of projects. This person will serve as an integral part of the Campaigns team, providing essential structural support and operational excellence. Crucially, this individual will also act as a critical point of contact and support system for Murmuration's external partners, ensuring transparent communication, aligned expectations, and efficient collaboration throughout the campaign lifecycle. Job Level: P4 What You’ll Do - Serve as the primary project manager for multiple, high-stakes campaigns, ensuring seamless coordination, precise execution, and transparent communication across all internal and external stakeholders; - Design, implement, and rigorously manage detailed campaign plans and timelines. This includes developing clear meeting agendas, capturing comprehensive notes, and executing proactive follow-up to ensure all campaigns and engagements are driven to successful, on-time completion; - Serve as the key operational contact for all external partners, expertly managing inbound inquiries and communication flow; - Provide strategic, trusted support and counsel to a diverse set of stakeholders—from grassroots student and family advocates to C-suite and senior organizational leaders—to maximize campaign effectiveness and partnership health; - Establish and maintain project management tools and templates to drive organizational efficiency and consistency; - Proactively identify, analyze, and mitigate potential risks and roadblocks that could jeopardize campaign timelines or outcomes; - Track, measure, and report on overall project health, presenting regular status updates to leadership; - Facilitate cross-functional retrospectives and post-campaign analysis to capture lessons learned and continuously improve future campaign strategy and execution; and - Manage budget tracking and vendor contracts. title: Senior Manager, Social
pay_candidate_snippets: Simple Mills was also a 2020 Health Magazine Snack Award Winner!
raw_description: Company Description Simple Mills is on a mission to transform the way food is made—creating nourishing products with astounding ingredients and amazing taste. Founded in 2012 by Katlin Smith, our brand has redefined center-aisle grocery by delivering better-for-you products made with unique, nutrient-dense ingredients. Today, we’re a category leader and the #1 natural brand in multiple segments, with distribution in over 30, stores nationwide. Now, as part of Flowers Foods, we’re entering an exciting new phase of growth—expanding our reach, accelerating innovation, and amplifying brand awareness, all while preserving the integrity of what makes Simple Mills special. Our commitment to using simple, high-quality ingredients ensures that every bite is both delicious and nutritious. Whether it’s watermelon seed flour in our cookies or butternut squash in our crackers, we craft our products with innovative, wholesome ingredients that deliver extraordinary taste. Our work has been recognized by Fast Company as a Brand That Matters and a Most Innovative Company, and has been featured in Vogue, Forbes, Women’s Health, and NPR’s How I Built This. In 2024, Inc. named us one of its Best Workplaces, reflecting our dedication to fostering an inspiring and inclusive environment where passionate individuals can make a difference. Join us as we shape the future of food. at www.simplemills.com. Role Description The Senior Manager, Social will play a pivotal role in shaping how Simple Mills shows up in culture, leading the -day strategy and execution of our organic social presence across platforms. This individual will translate brand and business priorities into a clear, differentiated social approach, guiding content direction and partnering closely with agency teams to deliver consistent, high-quality output. As a key member of the Integrated Marketing team, this role operates as a thought partner to leadership, contributing to direction while owning execution, performance, and continuous optimization. The ideal candidate is both creatively instinctive and analytically grounded, with a strong point of view on content, platforms, and what drives engagement. They are deeply attuned to cultural and consumer conversations, and able to translate trends in health, wellness, and sustainability into relevant, social-native storytelling. This role reports to the Senior Director, Integrated Marketing and responsibilities will include: Social Strategy & Channel Leadership - Shape and refine Simple Mills’ organic social strategy across Instagram, TikTok,, and (with Pinterest, YouTube, X, and Threads as secondary platforms). - Translate integrated marketing plans into platform-specific strategies, content plans, and success measures, ensuring clarity in what each channel is driving. - Develop TikTok Shop strategy and execution in partnership with external partners, ensuring alignment to broader social and business goals. - Identify and test opportunities to evolve channel approach, including new formats, tools, and platform capabilities, bringing forward data-informed recommendations. - Partner closely with Brand and Integrated Marketing teams to support launches, retail moments, influencers, and key initiatives. Content & Creative Direction - Lead content development in partnership with agency, ensuring output is strategic, insight-driven, and aligned to platform best practices, with a balance of hands-on input and directional leadership. - Guide development of monthly content calendars and production workflows, ensuring clarity in priorities, timelines, and deliverables (~40–50 assets/month). - Contribute to creative direction, developing repeatable formats, series, and storytelling approaches that build engagement over time. - Develop social-native creative ideas and content series in partnership with agency and influencers/creators that bring the Simple Mills brand and mission to life, translating complex topics (health, wellness, sustainability) into clear, engaging storytelling across formats. - Ensure a consistent, authentic brand voice while identifying and activating relevant cultural moments, contributing to content that resonates and drives engagement. Performance & Optimization - Define and track KPIs across platforms (e.g., engagement rate, reach, follower growth, video views, saves/shares), and own overall channel performance with a clear understanding of what is working and where to adjust. - Lead monthly and quarterly performance readouts, synthesizing key insights and translating them into actionable recommendations to continuously optimize content, cadence, and channel strategy. - Partner with paid media and influencer teams to amplify high-performing content and inform boosting strategy. Community & Agency Leadership - Oversee community engagement in partnership with our social agency, ensuring timely, on-brand interactions with the Simple Mills community (ie surprise & delights). - Leverage social listening and monitoring to track brand sentiment and identify emerging conversations, informing content and engagement opportunities. - Manage -day agency partnership, providing clear direction, feedback, and prioritization. - Monitor agency performance against defined scope and KPIs, identifying opportunities to improve effectiveness. - Perform other duties as assigned Simple Mills is a rapidly growing company on the forefront of the clean food movement, transforming center store grocery aisles with products made from nutritious, purposeful ingredients. Simple Mills is a female-founded business, started by Katlin Smith in 2012 out of her own Kitchen. In the company’s short history, Simple Mills has disrupted the market to become the #1 bestselling natural baking mix, the #1 bestselling natural cracker, and the #1 bestselling natural cookie. The company’s mission is to advance the holistic health of the planet and its people by positively impacting the way food is made. Simple Mills is distributed in 25, + stores nationally including Whole Foods, Target, Walmart, Kroger, Costco and more, and available online at retailers like Amazon and Thrive Market. The brand’s newest products include: Organic Seed Flour Crackers, Seed & Nut Flour Sweet Thins, and Soft-Baked Almond Flour Bars. Simple Mills has earned broad recognition from top tier media and industry associations- including a segment on our Founder & CEO Katlin Smith on NPR’s How I Built This. Our products have been featured in a wide array of top publications including Vogue, Women's Health, Forbes, Business Insider, mindbodygreen, NOSH and many more. Simple Mills was also a 2020 Health Magazine Snack Award Winner! Role Overview The Chief Environmental Officer (CEvO) will serve as the senior executive responsible for shaping and leading the organization’s environmental strategy, programs, and impact. This role requires a visionary leader with deep technical expertise and strong execution capability to drive large-scale environmental initiatives across vegetation development, land restoration, and sustainability. The CEvO will work closely with executive leadership and stakeholders to ensure alignment with national environmental priorities and long-term sustainability goals. Technical Authority - Act as the organization’s subject matter authority in environmental science, restoration ecology, and desertification control. - Review and approve scientific approaches, methodologies, and project frameworks. Stakeholder & Partnership Management - Build and maintain relationships with government entities, international organizations, and research institutions. - Represent the organization in high-level forums and environmental platforms. Governance & Compliance - Ensure adherence to environmental regulations, standards, and best practices. - Strengthen governance frameworks and reporting mechanisms. Team Leadership - Build, lead, and mentor a high-performing team of environmental experts and specialists. - Drive a culture of performance, accountability, and innovation. Ultimate Peaks is a premier executive search and workforce advisory firm, specializing in leadership hiring, strategic talent placement, and human capital consulting. Team & Job Overview EDC is seeking a Junior Associate, Climate and Sustainable Finance to join the Sustainability Team, assisting with the continued operations of EDC’s sustainable finance functions and the development of EDC’s climate and sustainable finance strategy. As a Crown Corporation, EDC has an important role in supporting businesses and large projects that contribute to Canada’s economy and international projects around the globe. EDC made a net-zero commitment in 2021 and is a member of the Net-Zero Export Credit Agencies Alliance (NZECA). We face a pivotal time of supporting industries and sectors of the future to increase Canada’s economic and climate resiliency while also balancing environmental impacts. To this end, the deployment of capital in line with EDC’s Sustainable Finance Framework, and the delivery of both economic and environmental or social impacts, remains a key component of EDC’s 2030 strategy. Students’ capabilities will be assessed against the requirements for the Sustainability team. Key Responsibilities may include: - Conduct transaction review and evaluation for eligibility against EDC’s Sustainable Finance Framework. - Assists with data collection, analysis and reporting towards EDC’s sustainable finance targets and the performance of EDC’s green bonds. - Assists with key performance indicator and sustainability performance target benchmarking against international environmental, social, and sustainable lending standards. - Assists in research to support the delivery of sustainable finance including frameworks, positions, market standards, etc. - Assists in preparing materials for senior team members or leadership. - Supports special projects (i.e. document management, data analysis, process design, content for internal awareness and education campaigns, stakeholder engagement etc.) Screening Criteria - Currently in or within 1 year of graduation from an undergraduate or masters degree in a relevant field, such as Sustainable Business, Sustainability and Financial Management, Environmental Science, Environmental Sustainability, Human Rights, Social Justice Studies or other relevant disciplines; - English proficiency: bilingual in both official languages (French and English) preferred. Assets - Experience in data analytics or portfolio reporting. - Experience working in sustainable finance (including portfolio monitoring, asset identification, and bond issuance). - Experience working in financial services or federal crown corporation. Location - Export Development Canada operates in a hybrid work environment, with a current requirement of two in-office days per week, increasing to three days per week in September 2026 (subject to change). - Opportunities may be performed from EDC’s headquarters in Ottawa or from one of our Community Hubs located in Toronto, or Montreal. The role Ember publishes the best-in-class dataset on global electricity generation and the data team is growing as we expand our datasets to new areas such as installed renewable capacity, price, battery storage, grids and flexibility, EV and heat pump deployment. We are looking for someone to use their data and coding skills to ensure we can quickly gather and curate data from new sources, as well as helping to run, maintain and document existing data pipelines. This role offers an exciting opportunity to learn from a knowledgeable and passionate team of engineers and analysts while applying your development skills towards the clean energy transition. About Ember Ember is an independent, not-for-profit energy think tank that aims to accelerate the clean energy transition with data and policy. We gather, curate and analyse data on the power sector and coal mine methane emissions, and use our findings to improve energy and climate policy. raw_description: Head of Marketing – Private Luxury Events Borough, South London (SE1 1EP) - Hybrid Fixed‑Term Contract until 30 June 2027 Private Luxury Events: Expect the Extraordinary Private Luxury Events delivers world‑class experiences to the luxury travel community through its event brands Amour, Private Luxury, TFest and Ultra. Our ethos has always been to put the human experience first. This mantra has powered some of the most respected events in the industry, inspiring thousands of luxury travel professionals around the world and at the heart of everything we do lies a passion for connecting people. Part of Worldwide Events Group Private Luxury Events sits within Worldwide Events Group, founded in 2004 and now a recognised leader in global MICE and luxury travel. Across our events, we bring people together and facilitate meaningful relationships, a philosophy we call H2H, human‑to‑human connection. Innovation drives our evolution. We’re embracing AI to elevate personalisation, streamline event design, and create smarter, more intuitive experiences for our global communities. Our Sister Brand: M&I M&I brings together high‑calibre meeting planners and exhibitors from the hospitality industry through a series of standout events across Europe, the Middle East, and the Americas. Our portfolio includes M&I Expo, M&I Flagship, M&I Healthcare, and M&I Luxe. The Role This is a fixed-term contract position (with the potential to become a permanent role) for an exceptionally creative, commercially minded, and experienced Head of Marketing. As Head of Marketing, Private Luxury Events, you will play a pivotal role in shaping the future of one of the most respected brands in luxury travel events, whilst supporting the development of our phase of growth. You will lead a talented marketing team of two and work closely with commercial, design and operational teams to deliver exceptional marketing campaigns that strengthen brand visibility, deepen audience engagement, generate qualified leads, and support commercial growth. This is a core generalist marketing role that combines brand stewardship, performance marketing, luxury industry relationship building, strategic partnerships, thought leadership, event marketing and team leadership. You will be responsible for developing a marketing function that balances long-term brand building with support for our commercial teams’ annual revenue and profit goals. Success will require equal confidence in analysing campaign data and conversion metrics, developing lead generation strategies, building luxury brand partnerships, launching new event concepts, and creating compelling content that resonates with senior decision-makers across the global luxury travel and luxury lifestyle sectors. This role requires a strong brand marketeer who will play a key part in expanding PLE's influence beyond luxury travel and into the wider luxury ecosystem. We are seeking someone who understands how luxury brands think, communicate, and collaborate, and who can position PLE as a leading voice not only in luxury travel but within the broader luxury landscape. As part of this, the role will support the development and future launch of a major new luxury lifestyle event connecting leading voices from luxury hospitality, design, wellness, travel, real estate, fashion, and luxury consumer brands. This is a player-coach role requiring both analytical and creative thinking with a hands-on approach. The successful candidate will be expected to remain closely connected to campaign delivery and to actively support and develop their team. Success in this role will depend on your ability to build trusted relationships, develop influential partnerships, create highly effective marketing campaigns, and elevate PLE as one of the most respected and influential brands in its category. You will report to the Director of Marketing, Worldwide Events initially for a handover period, and then to the MD, PLE. Responsibilities Marketing Planning - Working with MD PLE, translate PLE commercial goals into measurable marketing plans with clear ROI metrics. - Partner closely with sales, operations, and leadership teams to align marketing activity with business objectives, attendance targets, and revenue goals. - Develop tactical plans to increase brand visibility, audience engagement, and market penetration across key growth markets. - Lead -market planning and launch activity for new event concepts and strategic growth initiatives. - Identify opportunities to increase audience reach, brand influence, and commercial impact through innovative marketing initiatives. - Balance brand-building activity with measurable lead generation and revenue outcomes. Brand Campaign Management - Lead the development and execution of integrated brand campaigns across digital, email, social, content, PR, and partner channels. - Drive the successful positioning and promotion of PLE's global event portfolio. - Develop compelling campaign narratives that reinforce PLE's reputation as a premium and influential luxury brand. - Collaborate closely with design and content teams to ensure creative excellence across all marketing activities. - Leverage analytics, customer insight, and AI-powered tools to continuously optimise campaign effectiveness and creative performance. - Ensure all campaigns align with wider business goals and support commercial success. About the role Our client, is a systems change company working to accelerate the transition to a net-zero, nature-positive, and more inclusive economy. As a certified B Corp, they partner with business, finance, policymakers and civil society to transform five interconnected syst
raw_description: About the role Our client, is a systems change company working to accelerate the transition to a net-zero, nature-positive, and more inclusive economy. As a certified B Corp, they partner with business, finance, policymakers and civil society to transform five interconnected systems: energy, nature and food, materials and circularity, sustainable finance, and urban transformation. Founded in 2016, they have grown to a global team of more than 300 people across Brazil, France, Germany, Indonesia, Kenya, the Netherlands, the UK and the US. They are looking for a Strategy Associate to join their growing Sustainable Finance practice in Kenya, focused on public and development finance — strengthening governments' financing strategies and mobilising capital for climate, nature and development priorities, including sovereign debt sustainability and the case for investing in resilience. Working within small, collaborative teams, you'll support advisory engagements spanning finance ministries, central banks, IFIs/DFIs (including the IMF and World Bank), donors and the private sector, with opportunities over time to lead your own workstreams. raw_description: Background The Communications Officer is being hired under the Integrated Climate Adaptation Solutions for the Hindu Kush Himalaya Region (HI-CAS) project at ICIMOD, funded by Global Affairs Canada (GAC) – Department of Foreign Affairs, Trade and Development (DFATD). The project aims to improve climate-resilient, nature-positive livelihoods while strengthening the leadership and agency of rural women and Indigenous Peoples and Local Communities (IPLCs) in Bangladesh, Bhutan, and Nepal. The project is housed under Strategy Group Resilient Economies and Landscapes which focuses on delivering environmentally sustainable, but economically viable and socially inclusive solutions for some of the world’s most marginalised and vulnerable people. With a focus at both local and landscape levels, it builds understanding of the implications of rapid socio-economic, climate and environmental changes on mountain livelihoods and economies that are challenged by their remote, fragile, and hazard-prone settings. The project itself will be implemented through the adoption of gender-responsive and locally tailored climate adaptation solutions – grounded in feminist and human rights-based methodologies – that place the rights, agency, and leadership of IPLCs at the centre. These evidence-informed Integrated Adaptation Solution Packages (IASPs) will combine springshed management, renewable energy technologies to power irrigation systems, and agrobiodiversity practices. They will be complemented by capacity building and knowledge sharing to drive institutional policy and action. These initiatives will also help to attract sustainable investments in climate action and development – particularly in the water, energy, and agrobiodiversity sectors – with a strong focus on women’s and IPLCs’ leadership. The HI-CAS project will be implemented in two upazilas (sub-districts) in Bandarban and Khagrachari districts in the Chittagong Hill Tracts of Bangladesh; two gewogs (blocks) in Paro and Punakha dzongkhags in Bhutan; and two municipalities, Roshi and Dhankuta, in Nepal. Over its four-year duration, the project aims to benefit approximately 40, IPLCs and other vulnerable groups by reducing their exposure and sensitivity to climate change impacts while fostering ecosystem health and climate mitigation outcomes. Position Overview The Communications Officer will be responsible for boosting awareness of the outcomes and impact of the HI-CAS project by supporting the documentation and communication of the project results in line with the commitments ICIMOD has made in the HI-CAS Project Performance Measurement Framework, which is nested within our Strategy 2030: Moving Mountains and our Medium-Term Action Plan V (2023–2026): Embracing Change and Accelerating Impact and related Results Framework 2023-2026. It will also contribute to the wider communications efforts of ICIMOD’s Strategic Group: Resilient Economies and Landscapes, where the position sits. ICIMOD’s Communications Officers are creative, result-driven and motivated professionals who are passionate about the power of amplifying impact and driving policy and practice change through strategic communications, influencing and engagement. Working under the direct supervision of the Senior Project Coordinator HI-CAS, and co-supervised by the Head of Communications, the post holder will work closely with communication staff in the Strategic Group (and its respective Action Areas and Interventions) teams, and with the ICIMOD central Communications Unit, to deliver communication and knowledge products for the HI-CAS project. The role holder will ensure communications facilitate access to knowledge and the ability for ICIMOD to use evidence-based advocacy and influencing messaging in policy dialogues. All efforts will be guided by a strong GESI commitment, rooted in a feminist approach that challenges power imbalances, promotes women’s leadership, and centres the rights, voices, and knowledge of IPLCs. You will be focused on working directly with communities, partners, and ICIMOD staff to tell the story of HI-CAS through a variety of media. You will be tasked with amplifying community experiences and evidence generated by the project to inform wider advocacy efforts and drive the uptake of approaches used in the project. This is an exciting opportunity for someone who values delivering impact through written, oral, and visual communication and engagement approaches and methods, is passionate and experienced in feminist solutions for mountains and people, and is committed to helping build a greener, more inclusive, climate-resilient Hindu Kush Himalaya as ICIMOD moves into its next Strategy 2030 period. It will require very close teamwork and strong collaboration skills. The ideal candidate should have knowledge of feminist methodologies, GESI-responsive communication strategies, and experience working with IPLCs. Regional independent, inter-governmental non-profit knowledge organisation; acquires, creates, develops, exchanges knowledge related to sustainable mountain development. raw_description: ABOUT INKOMOKO Inkomoko supports entrepreneurs to grow their businesses in order to improve livelihoods, create jobs, and help communities thrive. In 2026, Inkomoko was listed by the Financial Times as the 5th fastest-growing company in Africa, supporting entrepreneurs across East and Central Africa to grow thriving businesses and build inclusive, resilient economies. Founded in 2012, Inkomoko has worked with more than 100,000 entrepreneurs, including thousands of refugee entrepreneurs. Inkomoko provides a combination of training, consulting, access to finance, and market-level systems change. We are the largest investor to refugee entrepreneurs in Africa. Inkomoko has + staff in 50 offices across Chad, Ethiopia, Kenya, Rwanda, and South Sudan. Through Inkomoko’s 2030 strategic plan, we are adding 3 additional countries to serve more than 550,000 entrepreneurs and growing our $30M loan fund to impact 7M lives. INKOMOKO VALUES All staff at Inkomoko are connected to a shared set of organizational values: ● Purpose: be solutions-oriented, produce high-quality work, be a global leader. ● Achievement: push yourself to reach beyond what you previously thought possible. ● Improvement: be humble, engage in continuous growth through open & accurate feedback. ● Bravery: willing to take risks, create a safe space for others, be compassionate, inclusive. ● We Eat Goat: we celebrate success and support each other in hard times. We do this work together in the spirit of turikumwe, tuko pamoja, abren nen, urang babarengan. ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY & RESPONSIBILITIES The Advocacy and Communications Manager leads country-level advocacy strategy and uses strategic communications to strengthen policy influence, public understanding and organizational visibility. Split between Advocacy (60%) and Communications (40%), this role bridges programmatic impact with strategic narrative shifts. The Manager actively engages in policy discussions, manages high-level stakeholder relationships, and drives advocacy initiatives to expand economic opportunities for refugee and host-community MSMEs. Concurrently, they strengthen national visibility, brand credibility, and storytelling impact by translating on-the-ground successes into compelling public narratives. Working closely with the Managing Director, the Regional Director of Advocacy, and the Regional Communications Team, the Manager ensures all policy efforts, media relations, and public campaigns are strategic, evidence-based, culturally appropriate, and aligned with Inkomoko’s global brand and risk frameworks. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES 1. ADVOCACY (60% TOTAL) A. Strategic Execution, Policy & Evidence-Based Advocacy (30%) ● Strategy Implementation: Lead the execution of the country advocacy strategy, ensuring coordinated, evidence-driven implementation that advances strategic objectives, influences policy outcomes, and contributes to overall programme impact. ● Policy Intelligence & Learning: Track and analyze regulatory and policy developments affecting refugee and host-community MSMEs, collaborating with the MEL team to synthesize research findings, data, and field insights into evidence-driven policy recommendations. ● Cross-Functional Alignment: Work cross-functionally with country program teams to ensure advocacy priorities are grounded in implementation realities and aligned across the organization. B. High-Level Stakeholder Management & Ecosystem Capacity Building (30%) ● Partnership & Coalition Building: Build and leverage strategic relationships across government bodies, donors, civil society, and the private sector to influence market actors, support investment partnerships, and promote inclusive financial regulation in refugee-hosting regions. ● Executive Representation: Support the Managing Director in representing Inkomoko at key external forums, preparing high-level briefings, analysis, and key messages to position the organization as a leading voice on market-based economic inclusion. ● RLO Advocacy Incubator: Lead the operational rollout of an Advocacy Incubator specifically for Refugee-Led Organizations (RLOs), strengthening their capacity to engage on priority policy and regulatory reforms. 2. COMMUNICATIONS (40% TOTAL) A. Strategic Storytelling, Policy Alignment & Digital Influence (20%) ● Evidence-Based Narrative Development: Identify, research, and develop compelling, data-driven client and programmatic success stories specifically designed to serve as qualitative evidence for policy change, strengthen donor trust, and shift public perceptions around displaced entrepreneurs. ● Targeted Content Packaging: Formulate and package field-captured assets into high-impact communication materials tailored for regional campaigns, national advocacy opportunities, annual reports, and donor-specific decks and reports. ● Strategic Digital Engagement: Develop and implement localized digital communications that amplify strategic partnerships, policy milestones, and organizational impact, ensuring alignment with regional brand and digital governance standards. ● Campaign Localization & Impact Tracking: Adapt regional campaigns to the South Sudan context, monitor digital engagement and campaign performance, and apply insights to strengthen audience reach and communications effectiveness. ● Institutional Representation & Events: Coordinate and lead strategic communications coverage for high-profile donor visits, partner engagements, and major corporate events to reinforce brand positioning. B. Brand Governance, Media Relations & Risk Management (20%) ● Regional Liaison & Alignment: Serve as the primary communications bridge between the South Sudan country office and the Regional Communications Team, securing necessary approvals and ensuring all local assets comply with global brand standards and strategic messaging. ● Proactive Media Relations: Cultivate and maintain an active network of local and national media contacts (print, radio, and digital). Draft high-quality media briefs, press releases, talking points, and Q&A documents to secure positive coverage. ● Crisis Communications & Risk Mitigation: Support country leadership in proactively identifying reputation risks, managing sensitive local incidents, and executing crisis communications plans in close coordination with the Regional Communications Team. ● Cultural Adaptation & Translation: Translate and adapt internal and external materials (incorporating local dialects like Southsudan Arabic where necessary), preserving the strategic intent, brand voice, and cultural appropriateness of the message. ● Field Brand Implementation: Coordinate the practical rollout of approved branding assets across field offices, client spaces, and events, supervising the visual quality of office signage, local materials, and vendor-delivered collateral. ABOUT INKOMOKO Inkomoko supports entrepreneurs to grow their businesses in order to improve livelihoods, create jobs, and help communities thrive. Founded in 2012, Inkomoko has worked with more than 60,000 entrepreneurs across East and Central Africa, including thousands of refugee entrepreneurs. Inkomoko provides a combination of training, consulting, access to finance, and market-level systems change. We are the largest lender to refugee entrepreneurs in Africa. Inkomoko has + staff in 40 offices across Chad, Ethiopia, Kenya, Rwanda, and South Sudan. Through Inkomoko’s 2030 strategic plan, we are adding 3 additional countries to serve more than 550,000 entrepreneurs and growing our $30M loan fund to impact 7M lives. INKOMOKO VALUES All staff at Inkomoko are connected to a shared set of organizational values: - Purpose: be solutions-oriented, produce high-quality work, and be a global leader. - Achievement: push yourself to reach beyond what you previously thought possible. - Improvement: be humble, engage in continuous growth through open & accurate feedback - Bravery: willing to take risks, create a safe space for others, be compassionate, and inclusive. - We Eat Goat: we celebrate success and support each other in hard times. We do this work together in the spirit of turikumwe, tuko pamoja, abren nen, Kula na sawa, On est ensemble. Inkomoko is an affirmative action/. Working closely with the Managing Director, the Regional Director of Advocacy, and the Regional Communications Team, the Manager ensures all policy efforts, media relations, and public campaigns are strategic, evidence-based, culturally appropriate, and aligned with Inkomoko’s global brand and risk frameworks. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES 1. ADVOCACY (60% TOTAL) A. Strategic Execution, Policy & Evidence-Based Advocacy (30%) ● Strategy Implementation: Lead the execution of the country advocacy strategy, ensuring coordinated, evidence-driven implementation that advances strategic objectives, influences policy outcomes, and contributes to overall programme impact. ● Policy Intelligence & Learning: Track and analyze regulatory and policy developments affecting refugee and host-community MSMEs, collaborating with the MEL team to synthesize research findings, data, and field insights into evidence-driven policy recommendations. ● Cross-Functional Alignment: Work cross-functionally with country program teams to ensure advocacy priorities are grounded in implementation realities and aligned across the organization. B. High-Level Stakeholder Management & Ecosystem Capacity Building (30%) ● Partnership & Coalition Building: Build and leverage strategic relationships across government bodies, donors, civil society, and the private sector to influence market actors, support investment partnerships, and promote inclusive financial regulation in refugee-hosting regions. ● Executive Representation: Support the Managing Director in representing Inkomoko at key external forums, preparing high-level briefings, analysis, and key messages to position the organization as a leading voice on market-based economic inclusion. ● RLO Advocacy Incubator: Lead the operational rollout of an Advocacy Incubator specifically for Refugee-Led Organizations (RLOs), strengthening their capacity to engage on priority policy and regulatory reforms. 2. COMMUNICATIONS (40% TOTAL) A. Strategic Storytelling, Policy Alignment & Digital Influence (20%) ● Evidence-Based Narrative Development: Identify, research, and develop compelling, data-driven client and programmatic success stories specifically designed to serve as qualitative evidence for policy change, strengthen donor trust, and shift public perceptions around displaced entrepreneurs. ● Targeted Content Packaging: Formulate and package field-captured assets into high-impact communication materials tailored for regional campaigns, national advocacy opportunities, annual reports, and donor-specific decks and reports. ● Strategic Digital Engagement: Develop and implement localized digital communications that amplify strategic partnerships, policy milestones, and organizational impact, ensuring alignment with regional brand and digital governance standards. ● Campaign Localization & Impact Tracking: Adapt regional campaigns to the South Sudan context, monitor digital engagement and campaign performance, and apply insights to strengthen audience reach and communications effectiveness. ● Institutional Representation & Events: Coordinate and lead strategic communications coverage for high-profile donor visits, partner engagements, and major corporate events to reinforce brand positioning. B. Brand Governance, Media Relations & Risk Management (20%) ● Regional Liaison & Alignment: Serve as the primary communications bridge between the South Sudan country office and the Regional Communications Team, securing necessary approvals and ensuring all local assets comply with global brand standards and strategic messaging. ● Proactive Media Relations: Cultivate and maintain an active network of local and national media contacts (print, radio, and digital). Draft high-quality media briefs, press releases, talking points, and Q&A documents to secure positive coverage. ● Crisis Communications & Risk Mitigation: Support country leadership in proactively identifying reputation risks, managing sensitive local incidents, and executing crisis communications plans in close coordination with the Regional Communications Team. ● Cultural Adaptation & Translation: Translate and adapt internal and external materials (incorporating local dialects like Southsudan Arabic where necessary), preserving the strategic intent, brand voice, and cultural appropriateness of the message. ● Field Brand Implementation: Coordinate the practical rollout of approved branding assets across field offices, client spaces, and events, supervising the visual quality of office signage, local materials, and vendor-delivered collateral. ABOUT INKOMOKO Inkomoko supports entrepreneurs to grow their businesses in order to improve livelihoods, create jobs, and help communities thrive. Founded in 2012, Inkomoko has worked with more than 60,000 entrepreneurs across East and Central Africa, including thousands of refugee entrepreneurs. Inkomoko provides a combination of training, consulting, access to finance, and market-level systems change. We are the largest lender to refugee entrepreneurs in Africa. Inkomoko has + staff in 40 offices across Chad, Ethiopia, Kenya, Rwanda, and South Sudan. Through Inkomoko’s 2030 strategic plan, we are adding 3 additional countries to serve more than 550,000 entrepreneurs and growing our $30M loan fund to impact 7M lives. We do this work together in the spirit of turikumwe, tuko pamoja, abren nen, Kula na sawa, On est ensemble. Inkomoko is an affirmative action/. raw_description: veritree and Job Overview veritree is an award-winning climate tech start-up based in Vancouver. Launched in 2021, our technology measures and verifies the impact of global restoration efforts from the ground up. We are on a mission to plant 1 billion verified trees by 2030, collaborating with businesses, planting organizations, and consumers who believe in the transformative power of verified restoration projects to create real and meaningful impact for the planet, nature, and people. veritree is seeking a Director, Business Development to own New Customer Acquisition (NCA): the team and strategy that bring new customers to veritree. This is a senior leadership role for someone who has built and scaled outbound revenue engines, developed and coached people managers, and owned -market strategy end to end. You will lead NCA across three motions: Carbon (strategic enterprise accounts), Foundation (grant and philanthropic partnerships), and Traditional Outbound (net-new prospecting into new industries and verticals). You will also own the account-based outbound approach and the compensation structures, systems, and enablement that make the team perform. As veritree's product portfolio grows, our -market is evolving from selling a single solution (tree planting) toward more solution-oriented sales across multiple products and stakeholders. You will lead the team to solution-sell to champions, run qualifying calls, and generate pipeline through events. You will partner closely with Sales, Marketing, and Revenue leadership to turn a defined universe of high-value target accounts into qualified pipeline and closed revenue. This is a builder's role at a fast-scaling, mission-driven company: you will inherit a high-performing team and a mature outbound engine, and you will be trusted to lead, evolve, and grow both. 12 Month Key Outcomes (12m KOs) - Assume full leadership of the outbound BD team, developing the Team Leads while sustaining or improving current meeting and pipeline attainment. - Continue scaling a positive ROI business development function that includes recruiting, hiring, and onboarding to expand outbound capacity across all motions. - Grow qualified outbound pipeline by 75% over the period and deliver a reliable outbound pipeline forecast aligned to the annual new-ACV goal. - Own and maintain the outbound GTM strategy, account-based targeting framework, and quarterly scoring and commission structures with no disruption to team performance. - Advance the team's AI and GTM engineering agenda, shipping automation and AI-powered prospecting, enrichment, and reporting workflows that measurably increase per-rep output. What You'll Do Team Leadership & Development - You will lead, coach, and develop the outbound BD team, including the Team Leads - You will own hiring end to end: job descriptions, hiring design and decisions, onboarding, ramp, and ongoing performance management (including performance plans and calibrations with People Operations). - You will set individual and team goals, run cadenced 1:1s and pipeline reviews, and build a culture that is both high-accountability and high-support. - You will design and maintain the team's compensation architecture: base and variable structure, meeting and pipeline bonuses, team incentives, and Team Lead structures. - You will own org and pod design as the team scales, evolving the structure to match where the business is going. - You will build the team's evolving sales capability as the product portfolio expands, coaching reps to solution-sell to champions, take qualifying calls, and drive pipeline through events, moving beyond today's single-solution outreach. New Customer Acquisition & GTM Strategy - You will own the outbound -market strategy across all three motions: account-based targeting of strategic accounts and their CSR and ESG decision-makers, net-new prospecting into new industries and verticals through Traditional Outbound, and the Foundation grants channel. - You will evaluate and evolve the NCA -market strategy using current market trends and analysis of existing Closed Won and Closed Lost deals, doubling down on the segments and plays that convert and redirect away from those that do not. Enablement, Revenue Operations & GTM Engineering - You will direct the team's AI and GTM engineering agenda, partnering with our GTM Engineer to build AI-powered prospecting and enrichment, automated per-rep performance reporting, and workflow automation that scales the team's output. - You will own the sequence library, outreach templates, onboarding programs, and vertical playbooks. - You will partner with Operations to spec reporting, define deal-stage workflows, and build CRM (HubSpot) views for targeting, prioritization, and forecasting. - You will own the outbound pipeline forecast and the methodology behind it. Cross-Functional & Executive Partnership - You will partner with Marketing on ABM, content, and the event-driven outbound motion, including the event approval workflow between Sales and Marketing. - You will ensure clean, well-defined handoffs to Account Executives and Partnership Managers. - You will work directly with Revenue and executive leadership on pipeline strategy and high-value account outreach. raw_description: Have you dreamt of working with the world’s most ubiquitous tech company to shape its sustainability approach and communicate its progress? Perhaps you’re the right person to help develop the sustainability strategy of an apparel icon or a financial services leader? We’re looking for an Analyst to support our market-leading sustainability consultancy and work on our sustainability strategy and reporting clients. This is a unique opportunity to help us achieve our vision to ‘create a world that believes in business’. Analysts lift our understanding of the challenges our clients face from great to excellent. You will conduct primary research to identify insights, conduct in-depth reviews to present recommendations, shape clients’ content strategies, dive into strategy development, and ensure alignment to key reporting frameworks, such as ESRS, ISSB,UK SRS and GRI. Responsibilities Research - You’ll work with clients and strategists to define the brief. A good brief brings clarity to the task, the client’s needs and helps to define the research criteria to cover. - You’ll help define the scope of the project, including how the research will be conducted and which sources to use. It’s the Analyst’s responsibility to make sure the scope is neither too wide nor too narrow and to always work within the client’s budget and brief. - You’ll lead primary research assignments using a variety of methods, including document analysis, online tools such as Factiva and Pulsar, surveys, case studies, focus groups and interviews (face-to-face, telephone and/or online) as well as conducting desk research when required. - You will be AI confident and AI responsible, always adhering to RY’s AI policy, principles and usage practices e.g. human-led, always. In tandem, your knowledge of AI as both a channel and an audience will inform the value we create for and with our clients. Insight - An expert at analysing and interpreting data, you’ll identify patterns and unlock solutions. You’ll also advise how best to turn the research into useful insights that shape our direction and recommendations. - You’ll deliver research findings in a format that best fits the task, generally either a written report or presentation, that are informative and with a clear link to the point of view, using RY templates and following our signature style. Sustainability Reporting and Strategy In the reporting space, this work will involve: - Understanding reporting stakeholders and audiences, and shaping the report development accordingly. - Helping to shape the channel and content strategy (on and offline), theme and messaging, and strategic direction of reporting projects. - Shaping and reviewing report content and providing recommendations. - Liaising with the copywriters and creative teams to bring the report to life. - Making sure the report meets the requirements of the client’s chosen standards or frameworks, e.g. CSRD, GRI, UK SRS and ISSB. - In the strategy space, this work will involve: - Contributing to the development of meaningful double materiality assessments. - Shaping and delivering stakeholder engagement as well as goal and target setting. - Shaping sustainability strategies, including their identity and activation. - In the communications space, this work will involve: - Developing sustainability communications campaigns with topic deep-dives. - Creating sustainability communications guidelines and toolkits. Who we are We’re RY, an independent, London and Birmingham based, brand, marketing and communications agency. Our 200-strong team of specialists have been working with multinationals, start-ups, private companies and public bodies for more than 30 years. Together we tackle complex challenges for complex organisations by defining their story, communicating it simply, changing behaviour and delivering results. We provide services in identity, campaigns, reporting, sustainability and employee engagement – and we bring our work to life through film, experiences, print, digital content and platforms. We want to be the best place to work where the best work gets done. To achieve this, we need talented people: People who share our passion for getting to the heart of a problem and working as a team to deliver standout work; committed people who think ingeniously, make things simple and connect with others. Note to recruitment agencies: We have a dedicated in-house recruitment function and do most of our recruitment directly. raw_description: About us At Gridcog, we're on a mission to accelerate investment in the clean energy transition. We're a SaaS start-up of energy nerds building the best project modelling software around, used on everything from co-located solar and storage to microgrids and EV fleets. Our clients, many of the world's leading Developers, IPPs, Consultants and Energy Users, are putting hundreds of millions into the transition, and we help them direct that money into the right projects: the ones that make both commercial and environmental sense. Who we’re looking for: We're looking for an exceptional Executive Assistant to be the right hand to our Chief Commercial Officer and a force multiplier for the whole commercial team, which includes our Sales, Marketing, Account Management and Industry teams. You'll be the person who makes sure nothing drops, the CCO's time is spent where it matters most, the right things move fast and the commercial engine keeps running smoothly as we scale. You're highly organised, proactive and calm under pressure. You take ownership, get things done, and handle sensitive information with total discretion. This role puts you at the centre of Gridcog's commercial world, trusted with real responsibility and counted on to deliver. What You’ll Do as an Executive Assistant to CCO: Right hand to the CCO - Own the CCO's calendar and inbox: triage, prioritise, respond on their behalf where you can, and flag clearly what only they can do. - Protect their focus time and keep them ahead of what's coming. - Organise travel, events and logistics across our four locations and time zones. - Prepare meetings end to end: agendas, pre-reads, briefing notes, follow-ups and action tracking. - Help keep deals moving: prepare and coordinate customer proposals and contracts. - Pull together data requests, complete procurement and vendor documentation, and draft customer and prospect communications. - Work closely with the CCO to build and embed processes that enhance commercial team performance and effectiveness. Trusted with the sensitive stuff - Handle confidential commercial, customer and investor information with complete discretion. - Strong judgement where you can use context and situations to make the right call when things are ambiguous. You will also help develop, articulate, and evangelize BPI’s agency-wide approach to buying strategy, platform best practices, and technical execution. Additionally, you will conduct analysis into programmatic inventory, and vendor research to ensure BPI negotiates and executes highly effective, innovative, and market-leading media activations that drive measurable impact for our clients. - Starting Salary Range: $100,000 - $110,000 (+ annual bonus) - Expectation to work from one of our offices (Chicago, DC, NYC, SF, LA) at least 3 days a week What the -Day Looks Like Media Strategy & Execution - Able to run most mid-spend clients + campaigns independently. title: Freelance Videographers
raw_description: Freelance Role: Videographers More Perfect Union is looking to expand our network of talented videographers to film for us. We film all over the United States and have shoots nearly every week. Who: We are looking for videographers from across the country and from diverse backgrounds who want to help make videos on worker power, labor, and economic justice. Specs: Our videos are filmed in 1080p, 24fps, and are generally shot in LOG. Our Class Room videos are filmed in 4k, 24fps, and are shot in LOG. Required Equipment: - High quality camera that can shoot in 1080p and 4k - Wireless lavalier microphones - Lighting equipment Compensation: For half-day shoots (5 hours or less), our budget is generally between $600-$800. For full-day shoots, (5.5 hours to 10 hours), our budget is generally between $1000-$1500. We also pay for mileage for shoots that are farther than 50 miles away using the IRS mileage rate. Full day shoots also receive a $16/per diem. If you are interested in being put on our roster of videographers, please fill out the below form and be sure to include your portfolio/reel.
